content_faq:
Frequently asked questions

Thanks to Goan114 for compiling this guide and to everyone who tested and shared feedback.

Please read these answers first. If your issue is not covered, contact us through the QQ group or GitHub Issues.

What should I do about crashes, stuttering, a black screen, loading errors or lost touch input?

Try the following browsers first:

  • Android: use the latest Edge or Chrome. Via is not recommended. On Huawei devices, avoid Zhuoyitong and Via; try the system browser instead.

    On other Android devices, the system browser and other regional browsers are not recommended. They may work but can have bugs; Quark is known to lose touch input.

  • Windows: Edge (included with Windows), Chrome or Firefox.

  • On Windows 7 or earlier, use Supermium as an alternative.

  • On Apple devices, use your preferred browser.

If the issue persists in one of these browsers, please report it.

If an older browser cannot open the launcher, or the WebGL 2.0 check fails, see the device and browser compatibility guide, which covers Supermium installation and Chrome's OpenGL backend.

Where can I find controls, strategy guides and the story?

The site includes control instructions. After starting a game, click the “?” icon at the upper right to open them.

For the original manuals and story, see the Touhou Project supplementary documents.

For strategy and systems such as Cherry, visit the THBWiki strategy guide.

If you are new to Touhou Project's setting or gameplay, start with THBWiki. It explains the game systems in detail.

Can I save my game?

There are two meanings of saving in a shooting game:

  • Can you quit in the middle of a run and resume later with the same lives and state? No. The original games do not provide this kind of mid-run save. A run usually takes about 25 minutes.
  • Can you keep records such as clears and play time outside the current run? Yes. These records are stored in score.dat, and compatibility with the original game has been tested.

Save files are specific to each game. For example, a th06 score.dat cannot be used in th07.

Will more games be added?

See the launcher library for available games and the multiplayer lobby for games that support multiplayer.

Each new game needs its runtime, input, resources and multiplayer features adapted. Follow project announcements for progress.

Games referred to as “新典” will not be ported, because of copyright risk and the amount of work involved.

Fan-game adaptation progress is also shared through project announcements.

What if game resources will not download?

First, check that you are not using a VPN.

Also avoid extensions that take over downloads. Internet Download Manager and similar extensions may interfere with resource loading.

Once the site has opened successfully, the launcher can usually reopen or refresh offline, even if the server later becomes unavailable. Most modern browsers support this.

If downloading remains impossible, use an import package.

Multiplayer connection problems

Multiplayer combines P2P (peer-to-peer) connections with server relaying. If a connection fails, open “Check network” in the multiplayer lobby, review the results and retry.

Use each room’s current entry button and status to see whether you can join or spectate. Supported matches allow spectators to join after play starts; availability depends on the game and room capabilities.

Star the project!

If you enjoy this project, visit our GitHub repository and click Star. Your support helps us keep developing it!

content_multiplayer:
These rules apply to cooperative play in th06, th07, th08, th10, th11 and th15. Game-specific rules take precedence when they differ from the shared rules.

Common rules

Challenge mode

Bombs are set to zero and cannot be used. The life display becomes a death counter. Dying still drops resources and respawns the player normally; players do not become ghosts and the run does not end because of the death count.

Boss endurance and player count

Boss current HP, maximum HP and stage-script thresholds follow the original game. Multiplayer adjusts damage received by the boss:

  • 1 player: damage multiplier 1
  • 2 players: damage multiplier 0.75
  • 3 players: damage multiplier 2/3
  • When a player runs out of lives and becomes a ghost, the multiplier follows the remaining controllable players; boss HP is not changed directly.

Deathbomb window

The cooperative deathbomb window is twice the original window, retaining the original effects of shot type, bomb count and special states. th06 changes from 6 to 12 logic frames; th10, th11 and th15 from 8 to 16. th07 and th08 double their calculated native windows. The additional touch-input grace period remains.

Death behavior

When a player runs out of lives:

  • They become an uncontrollable ghost that drifts without shooting. Dropped items match the original final-death drops.
  • They can be revived through life transfer.
  • All ghosts revive after a stage clear.

When all players die:

  • A team wipe occurs only after every participant has entered the ghost/revivable state.
  • A synchronized buffer of 180 normal logic frames (about 3 seconds) follows.
  • The run then ends, without continues.

Shared controls and the end of a run

Any player can advance dialogue, pause or resume. Pausing stops simulation for everyone; pressing R while paused restarts the run for everyone.

The run ends after the team-wipe rescue buffer, a full clear or confirmed exit. Endings, result menus, names, replay saving and returning to the title are then controlled independently. After playing the last confirmed frame, spectators can choose a native replay slot, enter a name and save the complete multiplayer replay locally.

Automatic Power-item distribution

  • At the point of collection, red items target the nearest controllable player below full Power; when everyone is full, they target the nearest controllable player. Ties favor the lower seat number.
  • This also applies to collecting below the collection line. The recipient need not cross the line and is not limited by the 20-pixel manual-transfer range.
  • A player below full Power collects normally. If a full-Power player touches a red item, it flies to the nearest teammate below full Power. If everyone is full, collection is normal.
  • A flying item keeps its recipient, but retargets the nearest non-full teammate if that recipient reaches full Power. Ghosts and inactive seats cannot receive red items.
  • When the whole team is full, the game's original full-Power item and scoring rules apply.

Life transfer

To transfer a life:

  1. Move within 20 pixels of a teammate.
  2. The donor must release the fire button and hold at least 1 spare life.
  3. Tap Shift / Focus 5 times, with no more than 24 logic frames (about 0.4 seconds) between presses.

Effects:

  • The donor loses 1 spare life. A controllable recipient receives a homing life item and gains 1 spare life.
  • A ghost recipient revives.
  • Priority is: ghosts, then fewer spare lives, then lower seat number.
  • Holding counts as one press. Shooting, timing out or leaving range resets the count.
  • The third and fourth taps show L 3/5 and L 4/5. The fifth transfers a life; release Focus and tap 5 more times for another transfer.

Additional effects for a revived ghost:

  • Bonus lives alone do not revive ghosts; a teammate must transfer a life, or the stage must end.
  • Power becomes half of that shot type's maximum.
  • Bombs return to the initial count.

th06, th07 and th08:

  • Rescue does not clear bullets; the revived player gains 240 logic frames (about 4 seconds) of invulnerability.

th10:

  • Rescue does not clear bullets; the revived player gains 280 logic frames (about 4.67 seconds) of invulnerability.

Power transfer

To transfer Power:

  • Move within 20 pixels of a teammate.
  • The donor taps fire 5 times.
  • No more than 24 logic frames (about 0.4 seconds) may separate taps.

Effects:

  • A transfer counter appears above the donor from the third tap.
  • The corresponding Power is deducted, and equivalent homing items fly to the recipient.

Power systems and transfer amounts:

0–128 Power (th06, th07, th08):

  • Transfer 20 Power: 2 large P items and 4 small P items.

0.00–5.00 Power (th10):

  • Transfer 1.00 Power.

Limits:

  • The donor must hold the full amount required for one transfer.
  • The recipient must be below full Power.
  • Priority is lower Power, then lower seat number.

Unlock synchronization

To prevent different score.dat files from changing multiplayer menus:

  • Extra, Phantasm, characters, practice stages and th08 routes are unlocked in memory.
  • Save data is not written.
  • Only replays can be saved.

Rank adjustments

  • Dying or bombing reduces Rank less than in single-player.
  • The reduction is divided by player count.
  • This prevents simultaneous deaths from lowering difficulty too quickly.

Other rules

  • Spell captures and failures are shared.
  • Score- or point-item-based extends are distributed to teammates, subject to individual life caps.
  • In games with bombs, the initial count for each shot type is one below the original, with a minimum of 1.
  • Normal P-item drops scale with participants: 2× for 2 players and 3× for 3. th10 currently uses 1× for 2 and 2× for 3. Full Power items do not multiply.
  • Mid-stage life and bomb drops use 1× for 2 players and 2× for 3.
  • Nearby teammates and attached effects, including hitboxes and shots, become more transparent.
  • Spell-card portraits are removed; text declarations remain.
  • A player's bomb gives everyone the invulnerability designed for that bomb, except Marisa A in th11; see that game's rules.

th06 Embodiment of Scarlet Devil

th07 Perfect Cherry Blossom

Game-specific rules

Power-item distribution

  • Once one player reaches full Power, P items already on screen become Cherry items and retain their native movement and collection. Later red items prioritize non-full players under the common rules; after everyone is full, new red drops become Cherry items.

Cherry+ adjustments

  • With 2 players, the Supernatural Border threshold is 50,000 Cherry+.
  • With 3 players, the threshold is 75,000 Cherry+.
  • Cherry and Cherry+ are shared and Borders activate together. If bombing creates different Border timings, the first player's Border ending ends every player's Border.

th08 Imperishable Night

Game-specific rules

Human/youkai gauge and team state

  • Each player has an independent gauge and human/youkai form. Shots, bombs, deathbombs and team-specific actions follow the selected team.

Familiars

  • Whether a familiar can be attacked, and its visible attackable state, depend on the local player.
  • Familiars never deal contact damage.
  • Bullets fired by familiars still follow the host.

Time orbs and night time

  • Time orbs, night time and stage progression are shared.

Power items

  • Multiplied P drops spread upward separately. Small P items still give 1 Power; large P items give 8.
  • One full-Power player does not convert P items that other players still need.

th10 Mountain of Faith

  • P items on screen turn into point items only after every controllable player reaches full Power.

th11 Subterranean Animism

  • Native collection conditions remain. At full communication gauge, items at least 40 logic frames old can also be collected from anywhere; bomb, dialogue and other native collection paths still work.
  • Attracted items keep tracking their original collector, even below the collection line or near teammates. Red items choose recipients under the common rules and retarget the nearest non-full teammate when the recipient becomes full.
  • Normal P drops multiply with player count; Full Power items do not.
  • Marisa A's bomb does not grant teammates invulnerability.
  • Life fragments are shared and do not multiply with player count.

th15 Legacy of Lunatic Kingdom

Game-specific rules

Mode and team accounting

  • Supports 2 or 3 players, each choosing Reimu, Marisa, Sanae or Reisen. Uses Legacy mode; Pointdevice checkpoint retries are not supported.
  • Stages, enemies, spell captures, score, point-item value and chapter/total graze are shared. Lives, bombs, bomb fragments and Power belong to each player. The same bullet can count toward each player's graze; graze glow is no longer limited to one player.
  • Boss/midboss damage multipliers follow active players: 1, 0.75 and 2/3 for 1, 2 and 3 players. Ghosts are excluded. Ordinary enemy damage, boss HP and script thresholds are unchanged.

Life fragments and stored lives

  • Each qualifying chapter reward or collected life fragment adds 1 shared fragment, rather than 2 or 3 based on player count.
  • Chapter rewards use the displayed chapter bonus: default thresholds are 1,250,000 for 2 players and 1,500,000 for 3. Before starting, the host can choose 500,000–5,000,000, in steps of 250,000. The UI also shows the required graze at 100% destruction (threshold ÷ 5,000). The threshold locks at start and does not fall when a teammate becomes a ghost.
  • Normally, 3 shared fragments grant an extend. In Extra, each of the first 5 extends requires 5 fragments; no further fragment extends follow. Each player can hold at most 8 spare lives.
  • Ghosts share fragment and extend accounting and can store lives; an extend alone does not revive them. Death grants no extra fragment. Whole-life and whole-bomb items belong to their collector; bomb fragments remain individual.

Life transfer and rescue

  • Hold at least 1 spare life, move within 20 logic pixels, release fire and tap Shift / Focus 5 times with at most 24 logic frames (about 0.4 seconds) between presses. On mobile, turn firing off first, then tap Focus 5 times.
  • Ghosts have priority, followed by fewer lives and lower seat number. A controllable teammate receives a directed life item; a ghost revives in place. Every 5 valid taps transfers one life; holding counts once. Release Focus before the next set of 5 taps.
  • Rescue costs the donor 1 life, keeps the recipient's stored lives, restores half maximum Power and the initial multiplayer bomb count, and grants 280 logic frames (about 4.67 seconds) of invulnerability. Stage clears also revive ghosts; stage-reset revival grants 120 frames.
  • The third and fourth taps display L 3/5 and L 4/5. Nothing is deducted before transfer, or if the life-item pool is full.

Power values and gifting

  • A small P gives 0.02 Power in a 2-player room or 0.03 Power in a 3-player room. A large P remains 1.00 Power. Room size, not survivors, determines the value; original full-Power scoring remains.
  • Native drop counts do not multiply. Red items target the nearest non-full player both above and below the collection line. They keep their recipient in flight and retarget on death. Red items remain while anyone needs Power. Full Power fills only the collector.
  • Within 20 pixels, tap fire 5 times with at most 24 logic frames (about 0.4 seconds) between taps to give a large P to the eligible teammate with least Power. Mobile requires 5 separate fire presses; continuous firing does not count.
  • The donor needs at least 2.00 Power, spends 1.00 and retains at least 1.00 Power. Ghosts and full-Power players cannot receive it. Power is deducted only after an item spawns; if its recipient becomes a ghost, it returns to an ordinary drop.
  • The third and fourth taps show a large-P icon and count. Life-transfer prompts have priority. No Power-transfer prompt appears below the donation threshold.

Bombs and teammate protection

  • Each multiplayer life starts with 2 bombs; no-bomb challenge mode starts with 0. Bomb fragments remain. Normal single-player starting bombs are unchanged.
  • Reimu, Marisa and Sanae grant teammates 120 frames of invulnerability when bombing. Each update during the bomb, including the last, tops up teammates to at least 40 frames.
  • Reisen grants at least 30 frames when activating her shield or breaking any layer, including the last. A persistent shield protects only Reisen, not the entire team indefinitely.
  • This does not revive ghosts or shorten longer existing invulnerability. Reisen's shield break does not interrupt a mobile movement gesture already in progress.

Display, movement and replays

  • Each player sees only their own hitbox, including focused and always-visible hitboxes. Teammate hitboxes remain hidden during fading. Only drawing changes; collision and network state do not.
  • Teammates normally use opacity 160/255, or 72/255 within 48 pixels. The local ghost uses 112/255; teammate ghosts use 88/255. Attached shots use drawing copies for transparency without changing animations or randomness. Rescue progress gradually makes ghosts clearer.
  • Ghosts cannot attack, graze, collect items or be targeted. Per-frame bullet and moving-laser targeting also excludes ghosts and picks the nearest controllable player.
  • The 2P panel keeps fragment text and numbers with tighter spacing. The 3P panel removes life/bomb fragment text and numbers but retains icon-fill animations; accounting is unchanged.
  • During mobile dialogue, dragging moves the player when native movement is allowed. Tap to confirm; hold still for 500ms to skip. Dragging does not confirm, skip, auto-fire or double-tap bomb.
  • Multiplayer replays save every seat's character, seed, build identity and confirmed input. Playback requires a compatible multiplayer build; original single-player replays are not accepted. Spell timing uses confirmed logic frames, excluding network waits.
